title: Road of approach modelled from the sibling formations of the corps (history layer v6)
desc: No report of the Official Records read for the position ledgers (OR vol. 27) prints a road of approach for 56 leaf units (Longstreet's corps except Kershaw, Semmes, Wofford and Pickett's brigades; the Fifth Corps except the 20th Maine and Day's division) or for any formation above them. Each is drawn by the road that every documented sibling formation of its corps names (Chambersburg Pike for the First Corps, from Kershaw's report; Hanover Road for the Fifth Corps, from the 20th Maine row and Day's division report). The sibling formations may not have been on the road the unit used.
why: The record read so far does not state the unit's road; the primary sources are unread in part (EG-0005) and the Official Records give only some brigades' routes. Literal documentation of the road of these 56 units is not available from the repository.
searched: The four OR27 position ledgers (history/positions/positions_{A,B,C,D}.jsonl, 3,503 claims), every claim that names a road on the lines of command (APPROACH-AUDIT.md, data/sibling-review.json), the road-name concordance (library/ROAD-CONCORDANCE.md). Not yet searched: the regimental and brigade reports not in the ledgers, Busey and Martin, state regimental histories.
subst: Sibling-road rule (DEC-015): the units take the road documented for the other formations of their corps only if every documented sibling names the same road and no report on the unit's line of command names another road, a road the repository cannot place or a road outside the loaded ground (tools/sibling-rule.mjs, data/sibling-approach.json).
recon: A MODELLED road of approach (plausible-procedural). The unit's gate (never moved), its single-label Bachelder day position and its march from the edge of the ground are as for any other drawn unit; only the road, the minute at the edge and the place in the column are modelled.
marking: Card pill 'Modelled approach'; card text 'MODELLED APPROACH' with the siblings listed (report, page, printed words); provenance row 'Approach road (modelled)'; link to this entry; about panel paragraph.
impact: 56 leaf units (about 17,300 figures) in the First and Fifth Corps.
owner_q: Accept the sibling-road rule (DEC-015), reverse it (delete data/sibling-approach.json and the units return to open gaps) or require two or more documented siblings.
rec: Keep it as marked until the reports of the brigades are read; do not read it as history.

title: Faces, hair, facial hair, skin tone and body shape of every enlisted man (figure models)
desc: No record gives any enlisted man's face, hair, beard, complexion, stature or build (see EG-0001). The figure models generate every man from his manifest seed: 24 head shapes, 8 hair styles, 7 facial-hair types, 12 skin tones, 5 eye colours, 12 body shapes, stature 0.95-1.06 of 1.73 m. The mixes (facial hair 30/22/6/18/6/6/12 percent, hair colours, skin-tone weights, grey share 12 percent, coat-off share on 1-3 July) are tuning weights.
why: Literal 100% is impossible: individual appearance of the 165,000 men was not recorded. No anthropometric table, photograph survey or muster-roll physical description set was read for this task.
searched: kit/kit_specs.json (wear_states, no appearance data), PDF Part B.6 (dress only), render/PLAN.md G8 (variation targets). Not searched: enlistment descriptive rolls (height, complexion, hair, eyes are printed on Union enlistment papers: a possible source for sampled distributions), Gould 1869 anthropometry, CDV surveys.
subst: Seeded deterministic generation: the same man always has the same face; distributions are tuning parameters recorded in data/figures3d/TIERS.json (F-FACE, F-DIST-*, F-GAP-COMPLEXION).
recon: Generic adult male proportions with varied faces; no distribution is claimed to match any army or unit.
marking: Tier overlay glyph on every individual (EG-0001 marking); card text names the figure as a generated individual; TIERS.json F-FACE.
owner_q: Provide or allow the descriptive-roll sources (for example the printed height, complexion, hair and eye colour on Union enlistment records) so the distributions can be sampled from data; until then they stay tuning weights.
rec: Keep it marked until the source exists; do not read it as history.

title: Star count and arrangement of the US national colour
desc: The national colour is drawn with 34 stars on 13 stripes. No repository text states a star count for the flags at Gettysburg. The count rests on statutory reasoning recalled from memory (a star is added on the 4 July following an admission; West Virginia was admitted 20 June 1863, so 34 stars were in law on 1-3 July 1863): the lookup was NOT performed in this task. The arrangement (rows 6-5-6-5-6-6) is a plausible choice; period flags varied.
why: The record read so far does not describe any regiment's national colour; individual flags carried other star counts and arrangements.
searched: The repository (kit, PDF B.6, history layer): no star count. Not searched: the Flag Act of 1818 text, regimental colour catalogues (state flag collections), photographs of colours.
subst: A 34-star national colour; tier inferred (statutory reasoning) with the lookup recorded as not done.
recon: Stars and stripes with 34 stars in a plausible arrangement.
marking: Tier overlay on the flag; TIERS.json F-STAR-COUNT / F-STAR-ARRANGEMENT; FIGURES3D-NOTES.md.
impact: Every Union national colour drawn (the manifest gives a flag to a small share of men per unit).
owner_q: Run the lookup (statute text, state flag collections for the regiments' colours) so the count and arrangement can be documented per regiment.
rec: Keep it marked until the source exists; do not read it as history.

title: Union regimental and state colours, Irish Brigade flag device, cavalry guidon, colour-guard structure, flag sizes
desc: The repository holds no description of any Union regimental or state colour (kit item regimental_color_union: "pattern not specified in B.6"), no device of the Irish Brigade green flags (flag_green_irish), no guidon designation (guidon_swallowtail_cav: "unsourced in the notes"), no colour-guard structure and no flag sizes. The figures draw the national colour; the regimental colour is a hatched GAP-colour flag; the Irish flag is plain green with a hatched edge; the guidon is a swallow-tail with stars and stripes, no designation. Who carries a flag follows the manifest's "few" draw (a tuning weight), not a documented colour guard.
why: Regimental colours were individual objects; the repository has no catalogue of them.
searched: kit/kit_specs.json items and units, PDF B.6.2-B.6.15 (flags are generic). Not searched: state flag collections (Pennsylvania Capitol flag collection, New York State Military Museum), regimental histories, the NPS flag records.

recon: National colour (inferred star count) plus visibly marked gap colours.

title: Confederate First Corps morning of Jul 2: no Official Records hours for Hood, McLaws, Longstreet at headquarters
desc: No OR report gives an hour for Hood or McLaws reaching the ridge, Longstreet at Lee's headquarters (C-006), or Lee's attack order (C-008). Kershaw's OR report (p.366) says his brigade left camp about sunrise and halted until about noon, which does not fit the memoir for McLaws's division. Hood filed no report in the OR index.

Not read: Taylor 1875 statement, Law postwar essay, McLaws and Hood postwar writings, Bachelder collection.

recon: Carry the OR bounds, the memoir values and the plan clocks as separate scenarios; do not merge or choose.

They put the summons near 23:00 on 3 Jul, the conference to about 02:00, the head of the train moving near 16:00 on 4 Jul, Imboden leaving after dark, the head at Greencastle at dawn on 5 Jul and the train at Williamsport on the afternoon of 5 Jul.

recon: Documented with a participant source.
competing: 4 Jul about 16:00 (Imboden) / by 17:00 (Lee order) vs 5 Jul about 20:00 (W-RET)
marking: None needed beyond the scenario marker
impact: Wagon train animation and sound (wails of the wounded p.424)
owner_q: None.

title: Rights basis of the ACWII mod assets: verbal permission only; authorship of each file evidenced only by Subversion committer records
desc: The owner reported on 2026-11-11 that the mod licence was verified by phone with the mod maker and ordered the ACW models used. Recorded as: owner-reported verbal permission from the mod author, 2026-11-11; no written text on file. The mod author (Subversion author ACW_Primergy, ACWII, 2011) can license only files he made. The pack data carries Subversion records for 78 files (all committer ACW_Primergy, md5 equal to the committed bytes); a committer record proves who committed a file, not who drew it. Of 2,200 asset-pack files listed (213 Subversion and housekeeping files are read as evidence, not listed), 24 pass the evidence rules (tools/bt/acw/policy.py) and are shipped; every other file is listed with its reason in data/figures3d/acw/manifest.json.
why: No written licence, readme or credits exists in the archive (acw-leads ACW-L02); only the owner can obtain or record permission (standing owner rule: legal acts are owner-only).
searched: ACW.zip (sha256 8efdb262...c9ed): every .svn/entries (78 file records), mod_details.lua, localisation, launcher strings (read as text, never run). Not searched: the mod's Discord, manual or update pages (links found in the launcher; not visited).
subst: Only files with a committer record and no base-game marker are shipped; every unclear file is excluded and listed. The credit line is in data/figures3d/acw/credits.json.
recon: Procedural figures for everything not cleared; 24 mod-painted Confederate jacket texture sheets as lead swatches.
marking: Credit line "ACWII mod by ACW_Primergy and team (used with the author's permission)" in the product credits data; tier mark on every use; the mod is no historical evidence (ACW-L01..L31).
impact: Which soldier, officer, gun and horse models can be used (none today).
owner_q: Ask the mod author for a short written confirmation (an email is enough) that names which files are his own work and which derive from the base game (norwegian_ski_troops meshes, field_carriage and euro_cannon_barrel textures, the base-game Euro heads and equipment); with it the excluded files can be re-evaluated and shipped by re-running tools/bt/acw/convert_acw.py.
rec: Keep the evidence rules: exclude when unclear. Do not ship base-game derived meshes on a verbal permission.
